correctness.rationale: A monic quadratic T^2-e_1T+e_2 contains every coordinate at a critical point. For distinct nonzero roots, comparing e_1,e_2 forces both block sizes 1 modulo 3. The cubic coefficient on these blocks is (h u+j v)^3 with h=(a-1)/3 and j=(b-1)/3 modulo 3. Outside n=2 modulo 9, distinct nonzero solutions force h=j nonzero and v=-u, hence the two stated residue classes. Zero-valued and one-valued cases give precisely support sizes 1 modulo 9. Distinctness and formula are verified. A standard-library verifier exhausts all F3 projective points for n=3..11, but only the proof establishes the all-n algebraic-closure result.

originality.rationale: The claim classifies every isolated geometric singular point of the characteristic-three elementary symmetric cubic when n is not 2 modulo 9. Xie gives dimensions and only extremal positive-dimensional partition components, explicitly leaving smaller-dimensional components unclassified; the signed bipartition orbit, residue conditions and point counts are not implied by those results. Orzel and Cafure–Matera–Privitelli provide bounds and partition-space constraints only. Searches found no equivalent point census; historical priority remains qualified.
residual_risks: Unindexed older classification of finite singular points of elementary symmetric cubic hypersurfaces in characteristic three could contain equivalent counts.
The result is a reduced-support theorem, not a classification of embedded or nonreduced scheme structure.

value.rationale: This is a complete classification of an explicitly identified missing geometric component regime, rather than a generic bound or one isolated numerical check. It reveals two new signed point-orbit series and the 43 singular points in eight variables (35 non-coordinate), refining the known dimension-only result and providing exact support data for singularity-scheme and complexity applications.
